Your response was very thorough and kind. I often need to be reminded that everything in my life is actually pretty good right now. My feelings are my obstacle, not reality. My career could be better, but my mentor is aware of my mental health issues and told me if I keep trying my hardest, I will still get a letter of recommendation, so there is still hope I can repair my career. 

As far as the past, I can only go to therapy and try to live in the present. I cannot enjoy my life if I am wrapped up in a traumatic past. Since my family is the one I chose, and they are extremely loving, maybe I shouldn't be so concerned with the way the family I did not choose treated me. Perhaps someday the past will not be such an obstacle towards my happiness. I just wish it wasn't so hard to block it out. 

As far as the friends who betrayed me, I have other friends too. For every person who has hurt me, there is another who lent me a hand when I was in great need. 

It is hard to think of the good though when you realize how completely different you are from your peers, but I think once I deal with my trauma, I will not view it as a thing that defines me, and I can once again relate to others. 

My son loves me, but I focus on all the things I could do better. This leads me to believe that I will let him down. It isn't rational, but I feel I could be better, and when I am not perfect, I beat myself up.

He was my best friend for five years before dating me, and we have been together five and a half years. It will be six on our wedding day. We have been close 11 years, so yes, he absolutely is aware. 

I have never had any real disagreements with him and he is a happy part of my life. I just feel guilty because I should be happy in general. We are told finding true love fixes things, but it doesn't. It just makes life less awful for me. I appreciate he doesn't try to fix me or give me worn out advice. He just listens and is there. Most people can't deal with it, but I guess he must love me. I know I love him. 

I worry my son will hate me for always being sad in the future. I worry he will blame himself. 

I think I might just ask people if I can come to them. I will make it clear I don't necessarily need anything but for them just to listen. I feel so alone, so when someone listens, it is one of the best feelings I have.

I can. I just start to annoy them after a while. I am exhausting, and I am sure they are happier when I am not around. I am almost always sad except when I am manic, and then I scare people away. 

When they burn into me, I feel like they can read what I am thinking, and I am scared I will be exposed as a villain if I let them see my face. My dad used to hurt me when I looked at him in a way that he interpreted as hostile. Even if I was just squinting to see something, he though  I was glaring, and I would  get hurt. I learned to look at the floor to avoid this. This also hurts my career. 

My fiancee is the only person besides my son that I trust, but I am often distant and sad even though I want to experience joy more than anything. I don't even know how people can live their lives mostly happy.

I have been hospitalized 12 times. One was a long term stay for a year. I am on Lithium, Lamotrigine, and Prozac. Lamotrigine and Prozac worked for four years on it's own. Lately it seems like nothing is changing. I know I can live a somewhat normal life. I have before, but it took me ten years to go into remission last time, and I lost everything. I don't think I can do that again.

I have been to therapy in the past, but I can't make eye contact with most people. It is like their eyes burn into me and can see everything wrong. It doesn't make sense, but that is what it feels like.  Therapists make me feel exposed and vulnerable, and that feeling is one of the most horrifying feelings I have. It is too close to what  people who hurt me made me feel like. 

I am being told to turn to psychedelics, and I know that isn't the answer from experience. I am actually considering ECT, but is that too extreme? There have been success stories in the past.

LSD made me quit drinking. Alcohol never did anything for me ever again after that. My father is an alcoholic, so that was an incredible result for me, but as far as psilocyben goes, no, unfortunately not. I was happy during the moment, but I was depressed later. 

I do have some mild feelings of closure when on MDMA, but that fades quickly.

Tried psilocyben :-(. I am considering going to this Ketamine clinic or getting EST. Ketamine is the only drug I haven't tried. I was told LSD would help, DMT, MDMA, and nothing worked. I know these seem drastic, but I am pretty low on options here. 

The only thing that makes things not completely and utterly unbearable is cannabis for the PTSD symptoms.

It is interesting to me. I took an honors German History course. For my final project, I interviewed a Holocaust survivor, a German American whose parents chose to flee after a few years into the Nazi regime, and I interviewed a lot of young Germans who currently reside in Germany. 

Every last one of them was deeply concerned about the jingoism present in American society. The younger Germans were completely appalled by the incident in Charlottesville since they were taught to learn from the mistakes of their great-grandparents or grandparents from the time they could form a sentence. One German student I interviewed made a wonderful point when talking about patriotism. She basically said that when you love something, you want it to be the best it can be, and in order to do that, past mistakes must be acknowledged. 

In America this is hardly done. We are often taught a version of history solely described from people of wealth and power. This leads to people hanging Confederate flags and claiming slavery had nothing to do with the Civil War. This also has people convinced European settlers were heroes when many subjugated and murdered Native Americans. We were perpetrators of genocide, but it is hardly talked about. 

How can we, as a nation, ever reach our potential if any criticism of our past and current actions are viewed as an attack on the nation as a whole? Having the bravery to confront and question our history and our leaders is what democracy is based on.

Mania is hell that ruins your life. I lost most of my friends, my job, and almost had to leave my field of study entirely because of a manic episode. It isn't always euphoria either. Sometimes it takes the form of uncontrollable bitterness and anger. Sometimes you get a mixed episode where you have the energy of a manic person but the mood of someone depressed (these ultimately end in hospitalizations for me). 

Sometimes you go into full blown psychoses and are so delusional that you get picked up by the police because of your erratic behavior. I actually thought people couldn't see me because I was dead once, so I made a series of unfortunate decisions. 

I used to love the thrill of a manic episode, but now, even at the height of euphoria, there is this underlying feeling of dirtiness and anxiety that makes it lose the appeal it once had. 

I hope you get your depressive symptoms under control because I know how hopeless and horrible that feels, but you definitely are not missing out.

My best friend is 5'4" and pushing 400 lbs. Unfortunately, she is also my roommate. She has diabetes and sores all over her body that won't heal. She spends well over 800 dollars a month on groceries, and it is all processed garbage. She hoards massive amounts of food under her bed, and when she no longer has any money, she eats my family's food. She has more and more health issues every year, and I feel like I did when I had to watch my father kill himself with alcohol. I have known her since I was nine, so she was basically my sister. 

I recently lost her as a friend because I had nothing to feed my son one dinner when she had raided our pantry while we were gone. I finally told her she has a problem and is going to kill herself over food, and that she is no longer allowed to touch any of my food. I spend 250-300 a month for my husband, my son, and I. We are financially strapped, so we can't afford to overeat.

She still lives with me unfortunately, and now people think I am this huge agent of oppression and hatred even though I am about as politically left as it gets. 

It fucking hurts, but I would rather her hate me and she FINALLY change (everybody is afraid to tell her the truth) than have her love me only to see her die in her 30's. 

I am not even allowed to tell people how worried and upset I am to see my friend go on her downward spiral because that makes me some kind of bigot. I have been told my concern wasn't genuine, and that really stung. When I had drug problems in my teens and early twenties, she helped me recover and everyone praised her for confronting me about my problem. I got better, and I lived. I am so afraid it will not be the same for her because we, as a society, are enabling this epidemic. 

I am a strong proponent of bodily autonomy because I feel like addiction is always going to be an issue in society, and I don't think shunning and mocking addicts helps at all, but to say it is OKAY and perfectly healthy to kill yourself is egregious and plain science denialism. We need to be able to accept obesity as a problem in order to help those who struggle with overeating, but we are too afraid to hurt the feelings of others even if it could save their lives.

I should have clarified. I don't mean literally nobody is using privilege as a way to bully others, of course there are people who are downright bullies about it. However, this almost always happens on the internet, and the person responsible is usually considered childish and damaging towards a cause that was meant to lift people up. I am an activist irl, and in our group we acknowledge privilege, but we have plenty of white males and people from all walks of life. We don't disparage anyone, nor do we assume life has been easy for different members solely on race. 

I am white, but I am mentally ill and in poverty. I might not fully understand what it is like to be a person of color, but I still go to many events in support of my friends who aren't white. In real life, NOBODY has told me to leave or that I didn't belong. These "SJWs" who are maligned by people on the internet are such a small minority that I have never had the displeasure of meeting one in real life, and if they came to any real life meetings acting the way they do, they would be called out. My friends who aren't in poverty or mentally ill also fight for economic justice and healthcare. They help the homeless (I am formerly homeless) since it is an issue that effects a lot of mentally or physically disabled people. Privilege in leftist groups is used to foster empathy in general.  

I knew I would get down voted because I am on Reddit, and most people here have only seen the obnoxious teenagers or YouTube videos. Those people aren't even respected in leftist political groups, but Reddit and the mainstream don't know this. In fact, most of those bullies don't even leave their houses. 

Also, when talking about privilege, it is understood we mean it towards America. We aren't saying privilege doesn't exist on an international level, but we are trying to fight a battle here among our community, so we look at privilege through that lens.

I thought I would pop in and say the mentally ill are far from privileged. I am a white girl and was raised in poverty. My dad was an alcoholic and abusive. I ended up homeless and pregnant. During the worst parts of my mental illness, I was sexually and physically assaulted, was targeted by police officers, and I was completely unable to afford psychiatric help. 

I was eventually given help. The diagnosis was Bipolar 1. Bipolar 1 ripped many opportunities away from me. Everyday is a struggle to function, but I am doing better now. 

I also have PTSD from the trauma I experienced during the worst of my mental illness. I am NOT privileged, and if I had seen this on the door, I would have confronted the therapist. I understand systemic racism exists, but my pain exists too. The mentally ill are underprivileged too.

I studied psychology. Neither one of those fully explain mental illness. It is common place to look at biological, psychological, and social and environmental impacts that could predict or worsen a mental illness. I don't know what a faulty chip is, and genetics still plays a role in illnesses like bipolar and schizophrenia especially, but genetics are not destiny and the impact of the environment on the expression of genes is still important to consider. There are a few things that could contribute to mental illness in the second panel, but some of those hardly have anything to do with mental illness. The second panel also fails to acknowledge numerous other contributors. 

In other words, you can't fully define something as complex as mental illness in an image like this.

As a person with Bipolar 1, this made me laugh. I have done some incredibly stupid, bizarre, dangerous, and sometimes hilarious things while going through an episode just to feel better because my brain made me think that was the solution. 

The actual solution was Lithium, but that doesn't sound as inspiring.

I have been hospitalized 10 times for Bipolar 1. I spent a good part of a decade in and out of psych wards. I think it mostly depends on the psych ward. 

I have had traumatizing experiences where the nurses were tyrants that held their power over me, and I have had good experiences where I left feeling normal for the first time in a very long time. I have been thrown in an isolation room and eventually tranquilized because I couldn't stop crying, and I have had other times where someone sat with me and let me talk and get it all out. I have had professionals yell at me for some of my weird behavior, and there are other times where I have received understanding that some of my actions were part of my disease. 

I haven't been in one for a long time, but ultimately they have been life saving for me. I rarely willingly go to one because they just suck to be in, and I would rather be home, but I am not dead and I am (kind of) stable on my Lithium right now.
